PVExtractFromImageSettings.NodeTooltip:
Derive a plant skeleton from a 2D image. Works best with a black and white mask

Traces the outline of a 2D texture (e.g. a hand-drawn plant skeleton) and extracts a branch skeleton from it. Useful for quick sketch-to-3D plant authoring, or for creating stylized plants matching a concept image.
PVExtractFromImageSettings.FailedToExtractGrowthData: Failed to extract plant from image

PVExtractFromMeshSettings.NodeTooltip:
Derive a plant skeleton from a static mesh.

Traces the geometry of a Static Mesh asset and extracts a branch skeleton from it. Material filters let you keep only the bark/structural portions while ignoring leaves or other elements. Useful for converting hand-modeled trees into procedural skeletons that downstream nodes can grow and mesh.
PVExtractFromMeshSettings.NoMaterialsSelected: No materials to keep set. Output will be empty

PVFoliageDistributorSettings.NodeTooltip:
Place foliage meshes onto a meshed plant using hormone-based or parametric rules.

Takes growth data from a Grower plus a Foliage Palette and produces foliage instances (each instance = one foliage-mesh transform). Choose between two distribution modes: Hormone Based (uses the simulation's growth data — natural feel) or Parametric (gradient and ramp based settings for more artistic control).

PVFoliagePaletteSettings.NaniteAssembliesFoliageMesh: A foliage mesh [{0}] has Nanite Assemblies. Nanite Assembly foliage is not supported yet.
PVFoliagePaletteSettings.EmptyFoliageMesh: A foliage mesh [{0}] has zero bounds. This is not supported.
PVFoliagePaletteSettings.NullFoliageMesh: A foliage mesh is [None] or doesn't exist
PVFoliagePaletteSettings.NodeTooltip:
Define which mesh assets are used as leaves/needles/etc., feeding the Foliage Distributor.

Holds the list of leaf, needle, flower, or fruit meshes for this plant. The Foliage Distributor consumes this palette to scatter instances on the grown plant.

PVGraftDistributorSettings.NodeTooltip:
Distribute pre-grown sub-plants (grafts) onto a main plant's attachment points.

Takes the host plant's growth data plus a Grafter Palette and attaches sub-plant skeletons at chosen attachment positions. Distribution rules mirror the Foliage Distributor (parametric or hormone-based).
PVGraftDistributorSettings.FoliageDataRemovedFromSourceSkeleton: Foliage data removed from source skeleton

PVGraftPaletteSettings.MaskPinWithGrowthData: A mask pin is connected to growth data. It will be ignored
PVGraftPaletteSettings.NodeTooltip:
Collects pre-grown plant skeletons (grafts) into a single palette for the Graft Distributor. Each entry on this node exposes an input pin where a grown skeleton can be wired in. The Graft Distributor picks one graft per attachment point on the main plant, using each entry's Attributes to match against the point's sampled conditions.

Press Ctrl + L to lock/unlock node output

PVGravitySettings.NodeTooltip:
This node controls how generated vegetation responds to directional forces, mimicking natural phenomena such as the downward pull of gravity and the growth tendency toward the direction of the optimal light conditions.(phototropism)

Adds bending or uprighting effects after growth has completed. Distinct from the Grower's built-in gravity (which runs during simulation). Useful for tweaking the result without re-running the simulation. Mode selects gravity (downward pull) or phototropic (upward toward light).

PVGrowerBaseSettings.NodeTooltip: Press Ctrl + L to lock/unlock node output

PVGrowerFoliageSettings.NodeTooltip: Press Ctrl + L to lock/unlock node output

PVGrowerSettings.NodeTooltip:
Grow a plant from a seed point using hormone-driven simulation.

The core PVE node. Takes one or more seed points and runs a multi-cycle growth simulation that produces a branch skeleton. When no seed is provided a default is automatically produced internally. Configure every aspect of growth — phyllotaxy, gravity, phototropism, senescence, bifurcation, foliage — through this node's inline parameters or via Standalone Override nodes.

PVGrowthDataDiffSettings.NodeTooltip: Diff two sets of grwoth data
PVGrowthDataDiffSettings.DifferentHierarchy: Plant hierarchy is not the same

PVGrowthDataJsonImporterSettings.NodeTooltip: Imports growth data from a json file

PVGrowthDataLoaderSettings.NodeTooltip:
Load a saved Growth Data asset and emit each named variation as a separate output pin.

Loads a Procedural Vegetation Growth Data asset, which holds one or more named plant variations — each a complete grown skeleton with attributes. One output pin is created per valid variation in the asset.

PVImporterSettings.NodeTooltip: DEPRECATED: This node no longer produces output. Use the Grower or Extract from Mesh/Image nodes to create new growth data.

PVManualEditSettings.NodeTooltip:
Hand-edit individual skeleton points and branches in the viewport.

Provides interactive editing of a grown plant: translate/rotate selected points, or remove branches by clicking them. Useful for fine artistic adjustments that procedural rules can't easily express. Edits are stored as transforms on top of the original skeleton, so the source is non-destructively preserved.

PVMeshBuilderBaseSettings.NodeTooltip: Press Ctrl + L to lock/unlock node output

PVMeshBuilderSettings.NodeTooltip:
Build a 3D mesh from the plant skeleton with materials, displacement, and detail control.

Converts the grown skeleton into a renderable mesh. Configure mesh resolution, branch radius shaping, profile detail, displacement, skeleton noise, and material assignments.

PVMockTreeImporterSettings.NodeTooltip: Create Procedural Vegetation Skeleton based of the Mock Tree

PVObjectInteractionSettings.NodeTooltip:
Make the plant respond to collider volumes (avoid, trim inside, or trim outside).

Defines collision volumes the grown plant must respect. Each collider can avoid (branches grow around it), trim outside (keep only growth inside the volume), or trim inside (keep only growth outside). Useful for plants growing past obstacles, topiary shaping, or carving clearance volumes for windows/walkways.

PVPlantProfileLoaderSettings.NodeTooltip:
Load a saved Plant Profile data asset containing trunk shape.

Loads a Procedural Vegetation Plant Profile asset, which contains data defining the shape of a trunk.
PVPlantProfileLoaderSettings.MissingDataAsset: Preset data asset is not set

PVPresetLoaderSettings.NodeTooltip: DEPRECATED: This node no longer produces output. Use the Grower or Extract from Mesh/Image nodes to create new growth data.

PVRecomputeGrowthDataAttributesSettings.NodeTooltip: Recomputes all growth data attributes using the plant skeleton

PVRecomputePointScaleSettings.NodeTooltip:
Recompute each skeleton point's scale attribute (its radius along the plant).

Replaces existing per-point scale values with newly-computed ones. Useful after importing or hand-editing a skeleton where the scales are wrong, or to apply a consistent taper. Three modes: explicit trunk radius, max-scale auto-detection, or smooth tip-to-base taper.

PVRemoveBranchesSettings.NodeTooltip:
Remove branches that meet a criterion (length, radius, light, age, or generation).

Filters out branches based on a single per-branch attribute. Use to mimic natural pruning (shade-pruning short or thin twigs), to simplify a plant for performance, or to clean up the silhouette.

PVRotateBranchesSettings.NodeTooltip:
Rotate branches around their parent's growth direction.

Rotates the axillary branches around the apical direction of its parent branch. Use to spread or twist branches independently of the original phyllotaxy. Combine ramp curves to vary the rotation along plant or branch length.

PVSaveGrowerPresetSettings.CannotSaveInNonEditor: Can't save a grower preset in a non-editor build.
PVSaveGrowerPresetSettings.NodeTooltip:
Save the current Grower's configuration as a reusable preset asset.

Captures the upstream Grower's fully-resolved parameters (including any Standalone Override nodes' contributions) and writes them to a ProceduralVegetationGrowerPreset asset on disk. Use to share configurations across graphs or to build a library of your authored plants.

PVScaleSettings.NodeTooltip:
Uniformly scale a grown plant up or down.

Multiplies every point's position and scale attribute by a single factor.

PVSimplifySettings.NodeTooltip:
Simplify the plant skeleton by removing redundant points.

Reduces skeleton complexity by removing points that don't significantly contribute to the branch shape. Uses the Douglas-Peucker line simplification algorithm. Useful for performance optimization without changing the overall plant silhouette.

PVSlopeSettings.NodeTooltip:
Simulate vegetation growing on a slope.

Tilts a fully-grown plant to mimic real-world slope adaptation: the trunk starts growing perpendicular to the slope surface and gradually curves toward vertical as it gains height. Useful for placing vegetation on hillsides, cliffs, or any sloped terrain.

PVSubgraph.PVSubgraphCyclic: Subgraph '{0}' forms a cyclic reference back to the current graph.

PVSubgraphSettings.NodeTooltip:
Embed a reusable PVE graph as a single node.

Wraps a saved Procedural Vegetation graph asset as a node in the current graph. Inputs are forwarded to the subgraph; outputs are forwarded back. Use to share complex configurations across multiple plants, or to package frequently-used node chains into reusable components.

PVTrunkTextureSetupSettings.NodeTooltip:
Bake or load trim sheet textures for plant materials.

Generates trim sheet textures (or loads previously-baked ones) and outputs the trim sheet UV details that feed into the Mesh Builder's materials. Use Texture Create mode to bake fresh textures; switch to Texture Load to use baked output.

RenderDocPlugin.HelpMessage:
<LargeText>Hello and thank you for trying out the UE RenderDoc plugin!</>

This plugin will allow you to capture rendering operations in the engine, and inspect them using RenderDoc.
There are three ways of capturing a frame:
* You can press the <NormalText.Important>green capture button</> in the top right of any viewport.
* You can run the <NormalText.Important>renderdoc.CaptureFrame</> console command. This will work anywhere and is very useful for capturing frames in packaged builds.
* You can use the capture hotkey (<NormalText.Important>Alt+F12</>). Please note that the hotkey is only active in editor windows and Play-In-Editor sessions.

If you are having trouble with not getting enough data in your captures, consider checking out the capture settings.
They can be found under <NormalText.Important>[Edit]->[Project Settings...]->[Plugins/RenderDoc]</>. All settings have tooltips that detail what they do.

A good place to start learning graphics debugging in UE is the <a id="browser" href="https://docs.unrealengine.com/latest/INT/Programming/Rendering/ShaderDevelopment" style="Hyperlink">Epic Rendering FAQ</>
It contains information on what CVar/project settings you should set when debugging shaders to get access to as much data as possible.

If you have any questions or suggestions regarding the plugin, please contact me via email or my github page:
<NormalText.Important>temaran (at) gmail (dot) com</>

I would also like to give major shoutouts to BaldurK, the author of RenderDoc:
<a id="browser" href="https://github.com/baldurk" style="Hyperlink">https://github.com/baldurk</>
And Slomp, who has made many great contributions to the project:
<a id="browser" href="https://github.com/slomp" style="Hyperlink">https://github.com/slomp</>

SIKRetargetPoseEditor.AutoAlignTip_Label: Automatically aligns bones on source skeleton to target (or vice versa).
SIKRetargetPoseEditor.PoseAlignmentTooltipText:
Direction: aligns the direction of the bone to match that of the equivalent bone in the other skeleton. Uses the chain hierarchy to define a direction vector. 
Local Rotation Axes: aligns the local axes of the bone to match those of the equivalent bone in the other skeleton. May produce nonsensical results on skeletons with different rotation axes.
Global Rotation Axes: aligns the global axes of the bone to match those of the equivalent bone in the other skeleton. May produce nonsensical results on skeletons with different rotation axes.
Mesh: Generates a direction vector for the bone based on the principle axis of the vertices weighted to the bone.

SNiagaraStackRowPerfWidget.GroupHeaderUpdateGPUTooltip:
This is the total GPU runtime cost of the combined spawn and update script call.
There are no individual module costs because the gpu stats cannot be measured on that level.
SNiagaraStackRowPerfWidget.GroupHeaderSimStageGPUTooltip:
This is the total GPU runtime cost of the simulation stage script.
If the simulation stage has more than one iteration then this is the combined sum of all iterations.
SNiagaraStackRowPerfWidget.GroupHeaderEmitterTooltip:
This is the total runtime cost of the emitter script and its module calls.
Note that the module calls do not add up to 100% because the script itself has some overhead as well.
SNiagaraStackRowPerfWidget.GroupHeaderTooltip:
This is the total runtime cost of the script and its module calls.
Note that the module calls do not add up to 100% because the script itself has some overhead as well.
SNiagaraStackRowPerfWidget.GroupHeaderSpawnTooltip:
This is the total runtime cost of the spawn script and its module calls.
Note that the module calls do not add up to 100% because the script itself has some overhead as well.
When interpolated spawn is enabled, this also includes the cost of running the update script on the spawned particles.
SNiagaraStackRowPerfWidget.GroupHeaderSystemTooltip:
This is the total runtime cost of the system script and its module calls.
Since the emitter scripts are embedded in the system scripts, they are part of this cost as well and visualized in a different color.
Note that the module calls do not add up to 100% because the system script itself has some overhead as well.
SNiagaraStackRowPerfWidget.ModuleEntryTooltip:
This shows the module runtime cost in percent.
The displayed percentage relates only to the parent script, not the whole emitter.
The module cost does not include work from DI calls to other threads, e.g. async collision traces.
SNiagaraStackRowPerfWidget.EmitterEntryTooltip:
This shows the module runtime cost in percent.
The displayed percentages relate only to the parent emitter script, not the whole system script.
Note that the module calls do not add up to 100% because the emitter script itself has some overhead as well.
SNiagaraStackRowPerfWidget.SystemEntryTooltip:
This shows the module runtime cost in percent.
The displayed percentages relate to the full system script, which has the emitter scripts embedded.
Note that even without emitter cost, the module calls do not add up to 100% because the system script itself has some overhead as well.

STestSuite.WidgetDecoratorTooltip: With the <RichText.TextHighlight>Widget Decorator</> you can <RichText.TextHighlight>inline any widget</> in your text!
STestSuite.RichText.HowItWorks: What does it do? The SRichTextBlock uses a concept called Decorators to introduce new font styles, images, animation and even whole interactive widgets inline with the text. Slate comes with a couple Decorators out of the box: • Text Decorator • Image Decorator • Widget Decorator • Hyperlink Decorator What about options? Of course you can always introduce your own Decorators by implementing ITextDecorator. This will give you full customization in how your text or widget is styled. Besides the power of Decorators the SRichTextBlock comes equipped with Margin support, Left-Center-Right Text Justification, a Line Height Scalar and Highlighting. How does the markup work? Well the markup parser is customizable so you can adjust the markup anyway you'd like by providing your own parser. The parser that comes with Slate though uses a syntax very similar to xml. • <TextBlockStyleName>Your text content</> • <img src="SlateBrushStyleName"/> • <a id="YourCustomId"/>Your hyperlink text</> If you ever want to use the markup syntax as actual text you can escape the markup using xml style escapes. For example: • < < • > > • " " But you only need to escape these characters when a set of them match actual syntax so this isn't generally an issue. Are there any catches? There are still plenty of things the SRichTextBlock doesn't currently support. The most notable lacking feature is not having the ability to flow text around images or widgets.
STestSuite.RichTextEdit.HowItWorks:
<RichText.TextHighlight>SMultiLineEditableText</> utilizes the power of text marshallers to control how the source text is displayed, and the two editors below are demonstrating the <RichText.TextHighlight>FRichTextLayoutMarshaller</> and <RichText.TextHighlight>FRichTextSyntaxHighlighterTextLayoutMarshaller</> implementations.

You can use the toolbar to control the style of the text in the rich-text editor, or you can directly edit the source text (demonstrating live injection of style information) to update the rich-text view.

SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.InteractiveEditModeTooltip:
Add: applies the current weight plus the flood value to the new weight.
Multiply: applies the current weight multiplied by the flood value to the new weight.
This operation applies interactively while dragging the slider. It operates on the currently selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.AddButtonTooltip:
Add: applies the current weight plus the flood value to the new weight.
This operation applies to the currently selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.AddWeightsSliderToolTip: Adjust the value to Add to the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.ReplaceWeightsSliderToolTip: Adjust the value to Replace on the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.WeightColorTooltip:
Adjust the weight display in the viewport.

Greyscale: Displays weights on the current bone by blending from black (0) to white (1).
Ramp: Displays weights on the current bone. Weights at 0 and 1 use the min and max colors. Weights inbetween 0 and 1 use the ramp colors.
Multi Color: Displays weights on ALL bones using the color of the bones.
Full Material: Displays normal mesh materials with textures.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.BrushFalloffTooltip: At 0, the brush has no falloff. At 1 it has exponential falloff.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.AverageWeightsSliderToolTip: Blend the amount to Average the weights on the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.RelaxWeightsSliderToolTip: Blend the amount to Relax the weights on the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.EditingModeTooltip:
Brush: edit weights by painting on mesh.
Mesh: select vertices/edges/faces to edit weights directly.
Bones: select and manipulate bones to preview deformations.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.SelectionSourceTooltip:
Choose which mesh to select components on (vertices/edges/faces).
Weights will be transferred from selected components on the source to selected components on the target.
If no components are selected on either the source or target, the whole mesh will be considered.
Source: The mesh to copy weights FROM.
Target: The mesh to copy weights TO (the main mesh in the tool).
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.ClampInfluencesButtonTooltip:
Clamp the number of influences to not exceed the target value.
Removes smallest influences first.
This command operates on the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.HammerWeightsTooltip:
Copies the weight of the nearest non-selected vertex.
This command operates on the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.CopyButtonTooltip:
Copy the average weights of the selected vertices to the clipboard. 
This is designed to work with the Paste command.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.FloodWeightsToolTip: Drag the slider to interactively adjust weights on the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.FloodSelectionTooltip: Flood the current selection by adding all connected components to the current selection.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.NormalizeWeightsTooltip:
Forces the weights on the selected vertices to sum to 1.
This command operates on the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.GrowSelectionTooltip: Grow the current selection by adding connected neighbors to current selection.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.PasteButtonTooltip:
Paste the weights on the selected vertices.
This command requires the clipboard contain weights from the Copy command.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.PruneInfluence: Prune the influence from the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.RelaxButtonTooltip:
Relax: the weight of each selected vertex is replaced by the average of it's neighbors. 
This smooths weights across the mesh.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.PruneButtonTooltip:
Removes influences with weights below the given threshold value.
Pruned bones are removed from the list of bones affecting the given vertex.
Pruned bones will no longer receive weight when a vertex is normalized.
This command operates on the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.ReplaceButtonTooltip:
Replace: the weight of selected vertices is replaced by the specified value.
This operation applies to the currently selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.EdgesTooltip: Select mesh edges. Ctrl-clicking converts the current selection to edges.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.FacesTooltip: Select mesh faces. Ctrl-clicking converts the current selection to faces.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.VerticesTooltip: Select mesh vertices. Ctrl-clicking converts the current selection to vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.BrushTooltip:
Select the operation to apply when using the brush.
Add: applies the current weight plus the Strength value to the new weight.
Replace: applies the current weight minus the Strength value to the new weight.
Multiply: applies the current weight multiplied by the Strength value to the new weight.
Relax: applies the average of the connected (by edge) vertex weights to the new vertex weight, blended by the Strength.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.NothingSelectedLabel: Select vertices on target mesh to edit weights...
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.BorderSelectionTooltip: Select vertices on the border of the current selection.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.InfluenceCountSelectionTooltip: Select vertices that are affected by at least N influences.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.AffectedSelectionTooltip:
Select vertices that are affected by the currently selected bone(s).
Holding Shift or Ctrl will add or subtract affected vertices from the current selection.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.WeightSliderToolTip: Set the weight on this bone for the selected vertices.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.IsolateSelectedTooltip:
Shows only the selected faces in the viewport.
Weight editing operations will not affect hidden vertices.
NOTE: This only works on the target (main) mesh.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.ShrinkSelectionTooltip: Shrink the current selection by removing components on the border of the current selection.
SkinWeightToolSettingsEditor.BrushFalloffModeTooltip:
Surface: falloff is based on the distance along the surface from the brush center to nearby connected vertices.

UE::Insights::NetworkingProfiler::SNetwo.Name_ColumnDesc: Type-stats category. Each row aggregates all UClasses sharing the same TypeStatsName tag in BridgeConfig (e.g. 'Vehicles' covers many vehicle classes). Untagged classes go into 'Undefined'.
UE::Insights::NetworkingProfiler::SNetwo.BandwidthWastePct_ColumnDesc:
Wasted Bytes / Total Bytes Serialized. Measures the cost of failures weighted by size. 
Low Send Waste % but High Bandwidth % indicates rare, expensive failures (object too large). 
Both high indicates large objects failing repeatedly. 
Shows N/A when there were no writes.
UE::Insights::NetworkingProfiler::SNetwo.PollWastePct_ColumnDesc: Wasted Polls / Polled. Object was dirty-checked but had nothing to replicate — wasted CPU. For push-based classes, high % means spurious MARK_PROPERTY_DIRTY with no actual state change. Shows N/A when there were no polls.
UE::Insights::NetworkingProfiler::SNetwo.SendWastePct_ColumnDesc:
Wasted Writes / Written. Counts failed serialization attempts by object, not by byte cost. 
High Send Waste % with low Bandwidth Waste % indicates many small objects failing (scheduling / priority). 
Both high indicates large objects failing frequently. 
Shows N/A when there were no writes.

UNiagaraDataInterfaceTexture.TextureSamplePseudoVolumeTextureDesc:
Return a pseudovolume texture sample.
Useful for simulating 3D texturing with a 2D texture or as a texture flipbook with lerped transitions.
Treats 2d layout of frames as a 3d texture and performs bilinear filtering by blending with an offset Z frame.
Texture = Input Texture Object storing Volume Data
UVW = Input float3 for Position, 0 - 1
XYNumFrames = Input float for num frames in x, y directions
TotalNumFrames = Input float for num total frames
MipMode = Sampling mode : 0 = use miplevel, 1 = use UV computed gradients, 2 = Use gradients(default = 0)
MipLevel = MIP level to use in mipmode = 0 (default 0)
DDX, DDY = Texture gradients in mipmode = 2

Wraps an underlying PCG Graph that emits scattered points. Useful for generating seed positions across an area. The configuration of the underlying PCG graph determines the scatter behavior — density, area, randomness, etc.

Convert PCG point data into Procedural Vegetation seed points.

Takes PCG point data as input and produces seed points the Grower can consume. Each input point becomes one seed; per-seed parameters can bias the initial growth direction to avoid nearby seeds or the cluster center, producing more naturally spaced plant populations.

USDLevelSequenceHelper.SnappedSectionTitleSubText:
In USD, start and endTimeCodes from any layer but the root layer are mostly ignored, while in UE a subsequence section range does clip the underlying animation.

In order to reconcile the behavior, subsequence sections on any of the StageActor's generated LevelSequences will automatically snap to the stage's playback range instead, which prevents any unwanted animation clipping.

UnrealMultiUserUI.FArchivedConcertSessio.UnmuteWarning:
Unmuting is not always safe
Pay attention if this session had muted activities, was unarchived, and now you're unmuting said activities again.

Example of conflict:
1. Create package Foo
Now mute 1 and unarchive session.
1. Create package Foo (muted)
2. Create package Foo
Archive the session, and try to unmute 1. You'd end up with a history that creates Foo twice, which is not valid.

Similar invalid cases can happen with transaction activities.
